source.text: Ἀρχὴ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: [The] beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

en.L: [The] beginning of the gospel of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: The beginning of the gospel about Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: This is how the good news about Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} began.

es.L: [El] comienzo del evangelio de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Comienzo del evangelio acerca de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Así comenzó la buena noticia acerca de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.

sw.L: Mwanzo wa Injili ya Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Mwanzo wa Injili kuhusu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo habari njema kuhusu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ilivyoanza.

decisions.choice: a title: the opening words name what follows
alternatives: the first sentence of the story itself
decisions.reason: The line has no verb. It stands at the head of the book, or at least of its first part (1:2-13), and says where the good news begins: with John in the wilderness and Jesus' baptism.

decisions.choice: gospel: good news, the announcement of what God is doing
decisions.reason: The word means good news, used of a victory or a king's coming. Mark uses it for the message that Jesus proclaims (1:14-15). Only later did it become the name of a book.

decisions.choice: of Jesus Christ: the good news about him
alternatives: the good news that Jesus himself proclaimed
decisions.reason: Both are true in Mark, since Jesus proclaims the good news of God (1:14). Here, at the head of a story about him, Jesus is most likely the subject of the news.

decisions.choice: Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God promised
decisions.reason: Christ is the Greek for the Hebrew Messiah, the anointed one. Israel's kings were anointed with oil, and the prophets promised a king from David's line. In Mark it is still a title (8:29; 14:61).

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends the line at Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Many early and later manuscripts add "the Son of God", and Mark calls Jesus God's Son at key points (1:11; 15:39). A few early witnesses, including the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, lack it. Scribes could have added the title, or dropped it by skipping a run of similar abbreviated words. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the gospel about Jesus (B); the good news about Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: "Of" could mean either, so Balanced and Readable say "about" to give the sense the meaning note prefers.

decisions.choice: el evangelio (L, B); la buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording: "evangelio" where it names the message, and the plain "buena noticia" at Readable, as the English Readable says "good news" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Spanish writes "Jesus Christ" as one name, "Jesucristo"; the alternative gives the name with the title, as the English setting does (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: Injili (L, B); habari njema (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording: "Injili" where it names the message, and the plain "habari njema" at Readable, as the English Readable says "good news" (meaning decision m2).

source.text: Καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν τῷ Ἠσαΐᾳ τῷ προφήτῃ· Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου·

records.literal_gloss: As it has been written in the Isaiah the prophet, Behold, I send the messenger of me before face of you, who will prepare the way of you;

en.L: Just as it has been written in Isaiah the prophet, "Look, I send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, who will prepare {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way;
en.B: It happened just as it is written in the prophet Isaiah: "See, I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; he will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} road ready.
en.R: Long ago God spoke through the prophet Isaiah. He said, "Look! I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He will get the road ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

es.L: Tal como ha sido escrito en Isaías el profeta: «Mira, yo envío a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensajero delante de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} rostro, que preparará {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} camino;
es.B: Sucedió tal como está escrito en el profeta Isaías: «Mira, envío a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensajero delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}; él dejará listo {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} camino.
es.R: Hace mucho tiempo, Dios habló por medio del profeta Isaías. Dijo: «¡Mira! Voy a enviar a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensajero delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Él {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} preparará el camino.

sw.L: Kama ilivyoandikwa katika Isaya nabii, "Tazama, mimi ninamtuma mjumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mbele ya uso {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, naye ataiandaa njia {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}};
sw.B: Ilitokea sawasawa na ilivyoandikwa katika nabii Isaya: "Tazama, ninamtuma mjumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} akutangulie; yeye ataitayarisha barabara {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.
sw.R: Zamani sana Mungu alisema kupitia nabii Isaya. Alisema, "Tazama! Ninamtuma mjumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} akutangulie. Yeye atakutengenezea barabara.

decisions.choice: the quotation joins Exodus 23:20 and Malachi 3:1 with Isaiah 40:3 (1:3)
decisions.reason: These words come from Exodus 23:20, where God sends his messenger before Israel, and Malachi 3:1, where the messenger prepares the way before the Lord. Mark joins them to Isaiah 40:3 and names Isaiah, the prophet of the road through the wilderness, for the whole.

decisions.choice: in Isaiah the prophet, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts name Isaiah. Many later ones read "in the prophets", most likely because scribes saw that the first lines come from elsewhere. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: just as: the scripture is fulfilled in what follows, John's coming (1:4)
alternatives: just as: the scripture backs up the title in 1:1
decisions.reason: The sentence has no main verb of its own. It most likely leads into 1:4: John came just as it was written. It could also look back to 1:1, the beginning that scripture foretold.

decisions.choice: my: God speaks; you: the one who comes, Jesus; the messenger: John
decisions.reason: In Malachi the Lord says the messenger will prepare the way "before me". Here God speaks to another, "you", whose way John prepares. Mark tells the story so that this one is Jesus (1:9).

decisions.choice: my, your, you with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: God speaks ("my") to the one whose way is prepared, Jesus ("your"), so the pronouns take the reader's capitalisation setting. "He" for the messenger is John and takes none.

decisions.choice: It happened just as (B); Long ago God spoke (R)
decisions.reason: An English sentence cannot begin with "just as" and stop. Balanced supplies "It happened", following the meaning note. Readable says that God is the speaker, as the first person "my" shows.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}}
alternatives: spans only on the stressed pronouns (mí, ti)
decisions.reason: God speaks to the one who comes (meaning decision m4). Wherever the English marks a pronoun for God or Jesus, the Spanish possessive, the stressed pronoun and a clitic standing before the verb take the span; a clitic joined to the end of a verb ("síganme") cannot take a capital and has none. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives ({{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}})
decisions.reason: Swahili carries many pronouns inside the verb (akutangulie, atakutengenezea), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so only free pronouns and possessives carry the span. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English in this chapter.

source.text: φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ, ἐγένετο Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ κηρύσσων βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν.

records.literal_gloss: [The] voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare the way of [the] Lord, straight make the paths of him, \v 4 came John the [one] baptizing in the wilderness proclaiming a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.

en.L: [the] voice of one crying out in the wilderness, 'Prepare the way of [the] Lord, make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths straight,'" \v 4 John the Baptizer came in the wilderness, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
en.B: A voice is calling out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord, straighten the roads {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will travel.'" \v 4 Then John the Baptizer came on the scene in the wilderness, calling people to a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of their sins.
en.R: Someone is shouting in the desert: 'Get the road ready for the Lord! Make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} paths straight!'" \v 4 That messenger was John the Baptizer. He came to the desert and told people to turn away from their sins and be baptized, so that God would forgive them.

es.L: [la] voz de uno que grita en el desierto: “{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} el camino del Señor, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} rectas {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sendas”». \v 4 Vino Juan el Bautista en el desierto, proclamando un bautismo de arrepentimiento para [el] perdón de [los] pecados.
es.B: Una voz clama en el desierto: “{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} el camino del Señor, {{plural_you:enderecen|enderezad}} los caminos por donde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pasará”». \v 4 Entonces apareció Juan el Bautista en el desierto, llamando a la gente a un bautismo de arrepentimiento para el perdón de sus pecados.
es.R: Alguien grita en el desierto: “¡{{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}} el camino para el Señor! ¡{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} rectos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} senderos!”». \v 4 Ese mensajero era Juan el Bautista. Llegó al desierto y le decía a la gente que se apartara de sus pecados y se bautizara, para que Dios la perdonara.

sw.L: sauti ya [mtu] anayeita kwa nguvu nyikani, 'Andaeni njia ya Bwana, nyoosheni mapito {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}},'" \v 4 Yohana Mbatizaji alikuja nyikani, akitangaza ubatizo wa toba kwa ajili ya msamaha wa dhambi.
sw.B: Sauti inaita nyikani: 'Andaeni njia ya Bwana, nyoosheni barabara atakazopitia.'" \v 4 Kisha Yohana Mbatizaji alitokea nyikani, akiwaita watu wapokee ubatizo wa toba ili wasamehewe dhambi zao.
sw.R: Mtu anapiga kelele jangwani: 'Mtengenezeeni Bwana barabara! Nyoosheni njia {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}!'" \v 4 Mjumbe huyo alikuwa Yohana Mbatizaji. Alikuja jangwani, akawaambia watu waache dhambi zao na kubatizwa, ili Mungu awasamehe.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 40:3: the voice that prepares the Lord's road home
decisions.reason: In Isaiah a voice calls for a road through the wilderness, so that God can lead his people home from exile. The wilderness is where John appears (1:4).

decisions.choice: the Lord: God in Isaiah; the one John prepares for is Jesus
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the Lord is God himself, the divine name. Mark sets the words so that the one whose road is made ready is Jesus, who comes in 1:9.

decisions.choice: the Baptizer: a title, the one who baptizes
alternatives: John, who was baptizing in the wilderness
decisions.reason: With the article the participle is a name for John, as in 6:14 and 6:24. Many manuscripts lack the article or add "and" before "proclaiming", which makes it a description of what John was doing.

decisions.choice: a baptism of repentance: a washing that marked a turning back to God
alternatives: a baptism that itself made people repent
decisions.reason: Repentance is a change of mind and of the whole way of life (see 1:15). Being dipped in the river showed that a person had turned back to God.

decisions.choice: for forgiveness of sins: leading to forgiveness, which God gives
alternatives: because sins had already been forgiven
decisions.reason: The word "for" points to the goal: the people who turned back would be forgiven. Forgiving sins belongs to God (2:7).

decisions.choice: the Baptizer
decisions.reason: Mark's word here is "the one who baptizes", not the noun Matthew uses (Matthew 3:1). "Baptizer" keeps the difference, which the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: That messenger was John the Baptizer.
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the quotation and the story imply, that John is the messenger and the voice of 1:2-3.

decisions.choice: Juan el Bautista
decisions.reason: "Bautista" is the Spanish noun for one who baptizes and the title readers know (meaning decision m3); unlike English "Baptist" it names no church, so Spanish needs no new word as the English "Baptizer" does.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Preparen|Preparad}}, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}}
decisions.reason: Every plural "you", pronoun or verb, is the plural_you setting: the ustedes form (Latin America) by default, the vosotros form (Spain) as the alternative. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. This holds for the whole book.

decisions.choice: Yohana Mbatizaji
decisions.reason: The agent noun "Mbatizaji" (one who baptizes) gives the title exactly, as the English "the Baptizer" does (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: jangwani (R); nyikani (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in John 1:23: "nyika" is open, empty country, the closer word; Readable says "jangwa" (desert), which young readers know better, as the English Readable says "desert". The same in verses 12 and 13.

source.text: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία χώρα καὶ οἱ Ἱεροσολυμῖται πάντες, καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And were going out to him all the Judean region and the Jerusalemites all, and were being baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing the sins of them.

en.L: And all the Judean region and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
en.B: The whole land of Judea and everyone from Jerusalem kept going out to him. They confessed their sins, and he baptized them in the Jordan River.
en.R: People came to him from everywhere in Judea and from the city of Jerusalem. They told God the wrong things they had done, and John baptized them in the Jordan River.

es.L: Y toda la región de Judea y todos los jerosolimitanos iban saliendo hacia él, y eran bautizados por él en el río Jordán, mientras confesaban sus pecados.
es.B: Toda la gente de Judea y todos los habitantes de Jerusalén acudían a él sin cesar. Confesaban sus pecados, y él los bautizaba en el río Jordán.
es.R: La gente venía a él de todas partes de Judea y de la ciudad de Jerusalén. Le contaban a Dios lo malo que habían hecho, y Juan los bautizaba en el río Jordán.

sw.L: Na nchi yote ya Uyahudi na wakazi wote wa Yerusalemu walikuwa wakitoka kumwendea, nao wakawa wakibatizwa naye ndani ya mto Yordani, wakikiri dhambi zao.
sw.B: Watu wa Uyahudi yote na wakazi wote wa Yerusalemu waliendelea kumwendea. Walikiri dhambi zao waziwazi, naye akawabatiza katika Mto Yordani.
sw.R: Watu walimjia kutoka kila mahali katika Uyahudi na kutoka mji wa Yerusalemu. Walimwambia Mungu mabaya waliyoyatenda, naye Yohana akawabatiza katika Mto Yordani.

decisions.choice: all: a great many, the whole region in motion
decisions.reason: "All" stresses how many came, as people speak of a whole town turning out. Mark later says that the leaders did not accept John (11:30-31).

decisions.choice: were going out, were being baptized: a stream of people over time
alternatives: a single crowd on one day
decisions.reason: The verbs are continuous: people kept coming and being baptized.

decisions.choice: confessing: openly admitting their sins
decisions.reason: The word means to agree openly, to say out loud. Here it is the sins that are owned up to.

decisions.choice: the Jordan River: the river running from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea
alternatives: a pool or stream near Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Jordan was the border Israel crossed to enter the promised land (Joshua 3). John baptized in the wilderness stretch near Jericho.

decisions.choice: told God the wrong things they had done
decisions.reason: Readable says what confessing sins means in plain words. Confession was made before God, and the crowd heard it.

decisions.choice: los jerosolimitanos
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the single Greek word for the people of Jerusalem; Balanced says "los habitantes de Jerusalén".

decisions.choice: kukiri (wakikiri, walikiri)
decisions.reason: "Kukiri" is admitting something openly (meaning decision m3); "kuungama" is heard first as confession to a priest in church use.

source.text: καὶ ἦν ὁ Ἰωάννης ἐνδεδυμένος τρίχας καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσθων ἀκρίδας καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.

records.literal_gloss: And was the John clothed [in] hair of camel and a belt leathern around the waist of him, and eating locusts and honey wild.

en.L: And John was clothed [in] camel's hair and [had] a leather belt around his waist, and [he was] eating locusts and wild honey.
en.B: John's clothes were made of camel's hair, and he had a leather belt around his waist. He lived on locusts and wild honey.
en.R: John wore clothes made from camel hair, with a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts, a kind of grasshopper, and honey that he found in the wild.

es.L: Y Juan estaba vestido con pelo de camello y [llevaba] una correa de cuero en torno a la cintura, y [estaba] comiendo langostas y miel silvestre.
es.B: La ropa de Juan estaba hecha de pelo de camello, y llevaba un cinturón de cuero en la cintura. Se alimentaba de langostas y miel silvestre.
es.R: Juan se vestía con ropa hecha de pelo de camello y se ataba un cinturón de cuero a la cintura. Comía langostas, que son una especie de saltamontes, y miel que encontraba en el campo.

sw.L: Na Yohana alikuwa amevaa manyoya ya ngamia na mkanda wa ngozi kuzunguka kiuno chake, na [alikuwa] akila nzige na asali ya porini.
sw.B: Mavazi ya Yohana yalikuwa ya manyoya ya ngamia, na alijifunga mkanda wa ngozi kiunoni. Chakula chake kilikuwa nzige na asali ya porini.
sw.R: Yohana alivaa nguo zilizotengenezwa kwa manyoya ya ngamia, na mkanda wa ngozi kiunoni. Alikula nzige, ambao ni aina ya panzi, na asali aliyoipata porini.

decisions.choice: camel's hair and a leather belt: the dress of Elijah
alternatives: simply the clothing of a poor man
decisions.reason: Elijah is described as a hairy man with a leather belt around his waist (2 Kings 1:8). Malachi 4:5 promised that Elijah would come before the day of the Lord, and Jesus later says that he has come (9:13).

decisions.choice: locusts and wild honey: food found in the wilderness
alternatives: a special diet for a vow
decisions.reason: Locusts were clean food under the law (Leviticus 11:22), and wild bees' honey could be found in rocks and trees. John lived on what the wilderness gave.

decisions.choice: locusts, a kind of grasshopper
decisions.reason: Many readers do not know that a locust is an insect, so Readable says so, as in Matthew 3:4.

source.text: καὶ ἐκήρυσσεν λέγων· Ἔρχεται ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου ὀπίσω μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς κύψας λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And he was proclaiming saying, Comes the [one] mightier [than] me after me, of whom not I am worthy having stooped down to untie the strap of the sandals of him.

en.L: And he was proclaiming, saying, "One mightier than I is coming after me; I am not fit to stoop down [and] untie the strap of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals.
en.B: This was his message: "Someone stronger than I am is coming after me. I am not fit even to bend down and untie the strap of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals.
en.R: He told the people, "Someone much greater than I am is coming after me. I am not good enough even to bend down and untie {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sandals.

es.L: Y proclamaba, diciendo: «Viene el que es más fuerte que yo detrás de mí, de quien no soy apto para, inclinándome, desatar la correa de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sandalias.
es.B: Su mensaje era este: «Después de mí viene alguien más fuerte que yo. Yo no soy quién para agacharme siquiera a desatar la correa de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sandalias.
es.R: Le decía a la gente: «Después de mí viene alguien mucho más importante que yo. Yo ni siquiera merezco agacharme para desatar {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sandalias.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akitangaza, akisema, "Anakuja nyuma yangu aliye na nguvu kuliko mimi, ambaye mimi sifai kuinama [na] kufungua kamba ya viatu {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}}.
sw.B: Ujumbe wake ulikuwa huu: "Baada yangu anakuja mtu mwenye nguvu kuliko mimi. Mimi sifai hata kuinama na kufungua kamba za viatu {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}}.
sw.R: Aliwaambia watu, "Baada yangu anakuja mtu mkuu zaidi kuliko mimi. Mimi sistahili hata kuinama na kufungua viatu {{deity_pronoun:vyake|Vyake}}.

decisions.choice: the one coming after me: the Messiah, whom John does not name
decisions.reason: John points away from himself to one greater, who will baptize with the Holy Spirit (1:8). Mark's next scene shows who it is (1:9-11).

decisions.choice: untie his sandals: the task of the lowest slave
decisions.reason: Taking off a master's sandals was a slave's job. John says he is not fit to do even that for the one who is coming.

decisions.choice: after me: later in time
decisions.reason: The words can mean "behind", as a disciple follows a teacher, but here they mean that the mightier one comes after John's work.

decisions.choice: not fit
decisions.reason: The word means sufficient or fit for a task, and Matthew 3:11 uses "fit" for the same saying.

decisions.choice: no soy apto (L); no soy quién (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means fit or sufficient for a task, which the English renders "not fit". "No soy digno" (I am not worthy) is the familiar wording, but it is the word of John 1:27, not this one; Readable says plainly "no merezco".

decisions.choice: sifai (L, B); sistahili (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means fit for a task, as the English "not fit"; "sifai" says that, where "sistahili" (I am not worthy) is the word for John 1:27. Readable keeps the plainer "sistahili", as the English Readable says "not good enough".

source.text: ἐγὼ ἐβάπτισα ὑμᾶς ὕδατι, αὐτὸς δὲ βαπτίσει ὑμᾶς ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: I baptized you with water, he but will baptize you in [the] Spirit Holy.

en.L: I baptized you with water, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will baptize you in [the] Holy Spirit."
en.B: The baptism I gave you was with water; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
en.R: I used water when I baptized you. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."

es.L: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} bauticé con agua, pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizará en [el] Espíritu Santo».
es.B: El bautismo que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} di fue con agua; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizará con el Espíritu Santo».
es.R: Yo usé agua cuando {{plural_you:los|os}} bauticé. Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:los|os}} bautizará con el Espíritu Santo».

sw.L: Mimi niliwabatiza kwa maji, lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atawabatiza katika Roho Mtakatifu."
sw.B: Ubatizo niliowapa ulikuwa wa maji; lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atawabatiza kwa Roho Mtakatifu."
sw.R: Mimi nilitumia maji nilipowabatiza. Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atawabatiza kwa Roho Mtakatifu."

decisions.choice: I baptized: John looks at the work he has done
decisions.reason: The verb is past. John speaks of his baptism as done, set against what the coming one will do.

decisions.choice: baptize with the Holy Spirit: pour out God's Spirit on people
decisions.reason: The prophets promised that God would pour out his Spirit on his people (Joel 2:28; Ezekiel 36:26-27). The one who is coming will do what water only pictures.

decisions.choice: in the Spirit: the Spirit is what people will be plunged into
alternatives: by the Spirit, as the one who acts
decisions.reason: Water and the Spirit stand side by side as the element of each baptism.

decisions.choice: with water, in the Holy Spirit (L); with ... with (B, R)
alternatives: in water, in the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: The Greek has no preposition with "water" and "in" with "Spirit". Literal keeps the difference. Balanced and Readable say "with" for both, the natural English.

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲτ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη εἰς τὸν Ἰορδάνην ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in those the days came Jesus from Nazareth of the Galilee and was baptized into the Jordan by John.

en.L: And it happened in those days [that] Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized into the Jordan by John.
en.B: It was during those days that Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee, and John baptized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the Jordan.
en.R: During that time, Jesus came from the town of Nazareth in the land of Galilee. John baptized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the Jordan River.

es.L: Y ocurrió en aquellos días [que] llegó Jesús desde Nazaret de Galilea, y fue bautizado en el Jordán por Juan.
es.B: Fue en esos días cuando Jesús llegó desde Nazaret, en Galilea, y Juan {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} bautizó en el Jordán.
es.R: En ese tiempo, Jesús vino del pueblo de Nazaret, en la región de Galilea. Juan {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} bautizó en el río Jordán.

sw.L: Na ikawa katika siku zile Yesu alikuja kutoka Nazareti ya Galilaya, akabatizwa ndani ya Yordani na Yohana.
sw.B: Ilikuwa katika siku hizo ambapo Yesu alikuja kutoka Nazareti ya Galilaya, naye Yohana akambatiza katika Yordani.
sw.R: Wakati huo Yesu alikuja kutoka mji wa Nazareti katika nchi ya Galilaya. Yohana akambatiza katika Mto Yordani.

decisions.choice: it happened: the old biblical way of starting a new event
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the style of the Greek Old Testament and simply opens a new scene.

decisions.choice: Nazareth of Galilee: a small village in the hills of Galilee
decisions.reason: Nazareth is not named in the Old Testament and was an unimportant place (John 1:46). Galilee was the northern region, far from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: into the Jordan: Jesus went down into the river
alternatives: at the Jordan, on the bank
decisions.reason: "Into" pictures him being dipped in the water. He comes up out of it in 1:10.

decisions.choice: it happened (L only); John baptized him (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the old opening phrase and make John the subject, which reads more naturally.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀναβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος εἶδεν σχιζομένους τοὺς οὐρανοὺς καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα ὡς περιστερὰν καταβαῖνον εἰς αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: And immediately going up out of the water he saw being torn open the heavens and the Spirit as a dove coming down into him.

en.L: And immediately, coming up out of the water, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit like a dove coming down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The moment {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came up out of the water, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit coming down on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} like a dove.
en.R: Right away, as Jesus was coming up out of the water, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw heaven torn open. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the Spirit coming down on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} like a dove.

es.L: Y al instante, subiendo del agua, vio los cielos rasgándose y al Espíritu como paloma descendiendo hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: En el momento en que salía del agua, vio que los cielos se rasgaban y que el Espíritu bajaba sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} como una paloma.
es.R: En cuanto Jesús salió del agua, vio que el cielo se rompía y se abría. Y vio que el Espíritu bajaba sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} como una paloma.

sw.L: Na mara moja, alipokuwa akipanda kutoka majini, aliona mbingu zikipasuliwa, na Roho kama njiwa akishuka kuja kwake.
sw.B: Mara tu alipotoka majini, aliona mbingu zikipasuka, na Roho akishuka juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kama njiwa.
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akitoka majini, mara moja aliona mbingu zimepasuka. Akamwona Roho akishuka juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kama njiwa.

decisions.choice: immediately: Mark's word for moving the story straight on
decisions.reason: Mark uses this word more than forty times, eleven in this chapter. Often it means "at once"; sometimes it just carries the reader into the next event.

decisions.choice: torn open: a violent tearing, not a gentle opening
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when the temple curtain is torn from top to bottom at Jesus' death (15:38). Isaiah 64:1 asks God to tear open the heavens and come down.

decisions.choice: he saw: Jesus is the one who sees
decisions.reason: The subject is still Jesus, who is coming up out of the water, and the voice in 1:11 speaks to him.

decisions.choice: like a dove: the Spirit's coming down is compared to a dove
alternatives: the Spirit took the bodily form of a dove
decisions.reason: The words can describe the way the Spirit came down or what was seen. Luke 3:22 says it was in bodily form; Mark only gives the comparison.

decisions.choice: to him: the Spirit came down upon him
decisions.reason: The word can mean "into", but after a verb of coming down it is often "to" or "upon", as in Matthew 3:16.

decisions.choice: immediately (L); the moment (B); right away (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word for this Greek word throughout. Balanced and Readable vary it, so that Mark's quick pace does not become a repeated word in English.

decisions.choice: al instante (L); en el momento en que, enseguida (B); en cuanto, enseguida (R)
decisions.reason: Mark's favourite word for moving the story on (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps one wording, "al instante", every time, so the reader can see how often Mark uses it; Balanced and Readable say it as the sentence needs. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: mara moja (L); mara, mara tu, papo hapo (B, R)
decisions.reason: Mark's favourite word for moving the story on (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "mara moja" every time, so the reader can see how often Mark uses it; Balanced and Readable say it as the sentence needs. This holds for the whole chapter.

source.text: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν· Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν σοὶ εὐδόκησα.

records.literal_gloss: And a voice came out of the heavens, You are the Son of me the beloved, in you I was well pleased.

en.L: And a voice came out of the heavens: "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the beloved; in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I am well pleased."
en.B: Then a voice spoke from heaven: "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved Son. I take delight in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: Then a voice from heaven said, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, and I love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. I am very pleased with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

es.L: Y una voz salió de los cielos: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo, el amado; en {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} me he complacido».
es.B: Entonces habló una voz desde el cielo: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo querido. En {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} me deleito».
es.R: Luego una voz del cielo dijo: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Hijo y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} amo. Me das mucha alegría».

sw.L: Na sauti ikatoka mbinguni: "Wewe ni Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, yule mpendwa; ndani {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} nimependezwa."
sw.B: Kisha sauti ikasema kutoka mbinguni: "Wewe ni Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mpendwa sana; ninafurahishwa sana {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}."
sw.R: Kisha sauti kutoka mbinguni ikasema, "Wewe ni Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} ninakupenda. Ninafurahi sana kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}."

decisions.choice: you are my Son ... I am well pleased: Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1
decisions.reason: In Psalm 2:7 God says to his anointed king, "You are my son". In Isaiah 42:1 God delights in his chosen servant and puts his Spirit on him. "Beloved son" also recalls Isaac (Genesis 22:2).

decisions.choice: I am well pleased: a settled delight
alternatives: God became pleased at the baptism
decisions.reason: The past tense here states God's approval as a fact, not a change that has just happened.

decisions.choice: You are: the voice speaks to Jesus himself
alternatives: the voice speaks about him to the crowd
decisions.reason: In Mark the voice says "you". Matthew 3:17 has "This is", addressed to those present.

decisions.choice: Son with a capital letter
decisions.reason: The word is a title here, as in 1:1 and 15:39, so it is capitalized, as at Matthew 3:17.

decisions.choice: Me das mucha alegría, with no span
decisions.reason: "Contigo" joins the pronoun to the preposition, so Readable says the same delight with the pronoun inside the verb ("me das"); the sense of meaning decision m2 is unchanged.

source.text: Καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτὸν ἐκβάλλει εἰς τὴν ἔρημον.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately the Spirit him drives out into the wilderness.

en.L: And immediately the Spirit drives {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out into the wilderness.
en.B: Straight away the Spirit drove {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out into the wilderness.
en.R: Right after that, the Spirit pushed Jesus to go out into the desert.

es.L: Y al instante el Espíritu {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} echa fuera, al desierto.
es.B: Enseguida el Espíritu {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} empujó hacia el desierto.
es.R: Justo después, el Espíritu empujó a Jesús a ir al desierto.

sw.L: Na mara moja Roho anamtoa nje kwa nguvu kwenda nyikani.
sw.B: Mara Roho alimsukuma aende nyikani.
sw.R: Mara baada ya hapo, Roho alimsukuma Yesu aende jangwani.

decisions.choice: drives out: sends with force
decisions.reason: This is the verb used for casting out demons (1:34, 39). It shows urgency and the Spirit's power, not hostility. Matthew 4:1 and Luke 4:1 say "led".

decisions.choice: drives: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: where Israel was tested
decisions.reason: Israel was led through the wilderness for forty years and tested there (Deuteronomy 8:2).

decisions.choice: drives (L); drove (B); pushed ... to go (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Mark's present tense. Balanced and Readable use the past, as English tells a story.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (echa); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (empujó)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. This holds for the whole book.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anamtoa); past at Balanced and Readable (alimsukuma)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. This holds for the whole book.

source.text: καὶ ἦν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τεσσεράκοντα ἡμέρας πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ ἦν μετὰ τῶν θηρίων, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And he was in the wilderness forty days being tempted by the Satan, and was with the wild beasts, and the angels were serving him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in the wilderness forty days, being tempted by Satan, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was with the wild animals, and the angels were serving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He stayed in the wilderness for forty days while Satan tempted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He was among the wild animals, and the angels took care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus was in the desert for forty days, and Satan tried to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do wrong. Wild animals were there with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and angels took care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y estuvo en el desierto durante cuarenta días, siendo tentado por Satanás; y estaba entre los animales salvajes, y los ángeles {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} atendían.
es.B: Permaneció en el desierto cuarenta días, mientras Satanás {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} tentaba. Estaba entre animales salvajes, y los ángeles {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} cuidaban.
es.R: Jesús estuvo en el desierto cuarenta días, y Satanás trató de hacer que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hiciera algo malo. Había animales salvajes con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y los ángeles {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} cuidaban.

sw.L: Naye alikaa nyikani siku arobaini, akijaribiwa na Shetani, tena alikuwa pamoja na wanyama wakali, na malaika walikuwa wakimtumikia.
sw.B: Alikaa nyikani kwa siku arobaini huku Shetani akimjaribu. Alikuwa kati ya wanyama wakali, na malaika walimtunza.
sw.R: Yesu alikaa jangwani kwa siku arobaini, na Shetani alijaribu kumfanya atende mabaya. Wanyama wa porini walikuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, na malaika walimtunza.

decisions.choice: tempted: put to the test, here by one who wants him to fail
alternatives: only tested to show his strength
decisions.reason: The word covers both testing and temptation. Satan's aim is to make Jesus turn from God's way.

decisions.choice: Satan: the adversary, the enemy of God
decisions.reason: The name means accuser or adversary. Matthew and Luke call him the devil in this story.

decisions.choice: forty days: Israel's forty years, and the forty days of Moses and Elijah
decisions.reason: Israel was tested for forty years in the wilderness. Moses was on the mountain forty days (Exodus 34:28), and Elijah walked forty days to Horeb (1 Kings 19:8).

decisions.choice: with the wild animals: in dangerous, empty country
alternatives: at peace with the animals, as in Isaiah 11:6-9
decisions.reason: Mark does not say what the animals mean. They show how wild the place was; some read them as a sign of the peace of God's new age.

decisions.choice: were serving him: caring for his needs
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Simon's mother-in-law in 1:31. Angels brought Elijah food in the wilderness (1 Kings 19:5-7).

decisions.choice: tried to make him do wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what tempting means in plain words, as in Matthew 4:1.

source.text: Καὶ μετὰ τὸ παραδοθῆναι τὸν Ἰωάννην ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ λέγων ὅτι Πεπλήρωται ὁ καιρὸς καὶ ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ· μετανοεῖτε καὶ πιστεύετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And after the to be handed over the John came the Jesus into the Galilee proclaiming the gospel of the God \v 15 and saying, Has been fulfilled the time and has come near the kingdom of the God; repent and believe in the gospel.

en.L: And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of God \v 15 and saying, "The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent and believe in the gospel."
en.B: After John had been handed over, Jesus went into Galilee, proclaiming God's gospel. \v 15 "The appointed time has arrived in full," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "and the kingdom of God has come near. Repent, and believe in the gospel."
en.R: After John was put in prison, Jesus went to Galilee and told people the good news from God. \v 15 He said, "The time God promised has come. The kingdom of God is coming near. Turn away from your sins and come back to God, and believe the good news!"

es.L: Y después de que Juan fue entregado, vino Jesús a Galilea proclamando el evangelio de Dios \v 15 y diciendo: «Se ha cumplido el tiempo, y se ha acercado el reino de Dios; {{plural_you:arrepiéntanse|arrepentíos}} y {{plural_you:crean|creed}} en el evangelio».
es.B: Después de que Juan fue entregado, Jesús fue a Galilea a proclamar el evangelio de Dios. \v 15 Decía: «Ha llegado plenamente el tiempo señalado, y el reino de Dios está cerca. {{plural_you:Arrepiéntanse|Arrepentíos}} y {{plural_you:crean|creed}} en el evangelio».
es.R: Después de que metieron a Juan en la cárcel, Jesús fue a Galilea y le contaba a la gente la buena noticia que viene de Dios. \v 15 Decía: «Ha llegado el tiempo que Dios prometió. El reino de Dios se está acercando. {{plural_you:Apártense|Apartaos}} de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pecados y {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} a Dios, ¡y {{plural_you:crean|creed}} la buena noticia!».

sw.L: Na baada ya Yohana kukabidhiwa, Yesu alikuja Galilaya akitangaza Injili ya Mungu \v 15 na kusema, "Wakati umetimizwa, na ufalme wa Mungu umekaribia; tubuni na mwamini katika Injili."
sw.B: Baada ya Yohana kukabidhiwa, Yesu alikwenda Galilaya akitangaza Injili ya Mungu. \v 15 Alisema, "Wakati uliopangwa umetimia kikamilifu, na ufalme wa Mungu umekaribia. Tubuni, na muiamini Injili."
sw.R: Baada ya Yohana kutiwa gerezani, Yesu alikwenda Galilaya, akawaeleza watu habari njema kutoka kwa Mungu. \v 15 Alisema, "Wakati ambao Mungu aliahidi umefika. Ufalme wa Mungu unakaribia. Acheni dhambi zenu mrudi kwa Mungu, na muiamini habari njema!"

decisions.choice: handed over: arrested and put in prison
decisions.reason: Mark tells of John's arrest in 6:17. The same verb is used of Jesus being handed over (9:31; 14:41) and then of his followers (13:9), so John's path foreshadows theirs.

decisions.choice: the gospel of God: the good news that comes from God
decisions.reason: God is the source of the news. Its content is what Jesus says next: God's kingdom has come near.

decisions.choice: the time has been fulfilled: the time God set has fully come
alternatives: time in general has run out
decisions.reason: The word for time is the appointed moment. What the prophets waited for has arrived.

decisions.choice: has come near: it is close at hand, already pressing in
decisions.reason: The perfect tense says the kingdom has drawn near and is now close. Matthew 4:17 has the same verb. God's rule is breaking in through Jesus' words and works.

decisions.choice: believe in the gospel: trust the message and rely on it
decisions.reason: Believing "in" a message is an unusual phrase. It means putting one's trust in the news that God's kingdom has come near.

decisions.choice: was put in prison
decisions.reason: Readable says what being handed over meant for John, which Mark tells in 6:17.

decisions.choice: turn away from your sins and come back to God
decisions.reason: Readable says what repenting means, as in Matthew 3:2 and 4:17.

decisions.choice: el reino de Dios
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording at every level; "reino" covers both God's rule and the realm where it holds, as the Greek word does.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:arrepiéntanse|arrepentíos}} (L, B); {{plural_you:apártense|apartaos}} de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} pecados y {{plural_you:vuelvan|volved}} a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide term "arrepentirse"; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does, and as Matthew 4:17 does.

decisions.choice: ufalme wa Mungu
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording at every level; "ufalme" covers both God's rule and the realm where it holds, as the Greek word does.

decisions.choice: tubuni (L, B); acheni dhambi zenu mrudi kwa Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide term "kutubu"; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does, and as Matthew 4:17 does.

source.text: Καὶ παράγων παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν Σίμωνα καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν Σίμωνος ἀμφιβάλλοντας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλιεῖς·

records.literal_gloss: And passing by beside the sea of the Galilee he saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting in the sea; they were for fishermen.

en.L: And passing along beside the Sea of Galilee, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw Simon and Andrew, Simon's brother, casting [a net] in the sea, for they were fishermen.
en.B: As Jesus went along the shore of the Sea of Galilee, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw Simon and Simon's brother Andrew throwing a net into the water. They fished for a living.
en.R: One day Jesus was walking beside Lake Galilee. He saw Simon and his brother Andrew throwing a net into the lake to catch fish, because they were fishermen.

es.L: Y pasando junto al mar de Galilea, vio a Simón y a Andrés, el hermano de Simón, lanzando [una red] en el mar, pues eran pescadores.
es.B: Mientras Jesús iba por la orilla del mar de Galilea, vio a Simón y a Andrés, hermano de Simón, que echaban una red al agua. Vivían de la pesca.
es.R: Un día Jesús caminaba junto al lago de Galilea. Vio a Simón y a su hermano Andrés, que estaban echando una red al lago para atrapar peces, porque eran pescadores.

sw.L: Na akipita kando ya Bahari ya Galilaya, aliwaona Simoni na Andrea, ndugu yake Simoni, wakitupa [wavu] baharini, kwa maana walikuwa wavuvi.
sw.B: Yesu alipokuwa akipita ufuoni mwa Bahari ya Galilaya, aliwaona Simoni na Andrea ndugu yake Simoni, wakitupa wavu majini. Kazi yao ilikuwa kuvua samaki.
sw.R: Siku moja Yesu alikuwa akitembea kando ya Ziwa Galilaya. Aliwaona Simoni na Andrea ndugu yake wakitupa wavu ziwani ili wavue samaki, kwa sababu walikuwa wavuvi.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Galilee: a freshwater lake about thirteen miles long
decisions.reason: The Greek calls it a sea, following Hebrew usage, but it is a large lake. Fishing was one of the main trades of the towns on its shore.

decisions.choice: casting: throwing a round net by hand
decisions.reason: The verb itself means throwing around; it was used for a casting net, thrown from the shore or from shallow water.

decisions.choice: a net (L in brackets, B, R); Jesus (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "casting". Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the last sentence spoke of him only by "he".

decisions.choice: Lake Galilee
decisions.reason: Readable calls it a lake, which is what it is, as in Matthew 4:18.

decisions.choice: el mar de Galilea (L, B); el lago de Galilea (R)
alternatives: el lago de Galilea at Balanced
decisions.reason: As the English: the name keeps Mark's word "sea" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "lago", since it is a freshwater lake (meaning decision m1). The term sheet's "el lago" (B) is for "the sea" standing alone.

decisions.choice: Bahari ya Galilaya (L, B); Ziwa Galilaya (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the name keeps Mark's word "sea" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "Ziwa", since it is a freshwater lake (meaning decision m1).

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου, καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς γενέσθαι ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων.

records.literal_gloss: And said to them the Jesus, Come after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "Come after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will make you become fishers of {{gender:people|men}}."
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Come and follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will make you into fishers of {{gender:people|men}}."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Come, follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will teach you to catch {{gender:people|men}} instead of fish."

es.L: Y les dijo Jesús: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} detrás de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y {{plural_you:los|os}} haré llegar a ser pescadores de {{gender:personas|hombres}}».
es.B: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} y {{plural_you:síganme|seguidme}}. Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} haré pescadores de {{gender:personas|hombres}}».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, {{plural_you:síganme|seguidme}}. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} enseñaré a pescar {{gender:personas|hombres}} en lugar de peces».

sw.L: Na Yesu akawaambia, "Njooni nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawafanya kuwa wavuvi wa watu."
sw.B: Yesu aliwaambia, "Njooni mnifuate. Nitawafanya muwe wavuvi wa watu."
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Njooni, mnifuate. Nitawafundisha kuvua watu badala ya samaki."

decisions.choice: come after me: become my disciples, following me as your teacher
alternatives: walk behind me for a while
decisions.reason: Disciples walked behind their teacher, learning from him as they went.

decisions.choice: fishers of people: they will gather people for God's kingdom
alternatives: a threat of judgment, as fishing is in Jeremiah 16:16
decisions.reason: Jesus takes their trade as a picture of their new work, bringing people in to God's kingdom.

decisions.choice: men: human beings
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for human beings, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: I will make you become: they will grow into this work
alternatives: they are fishers of people at once
decisions.reason: Mark has "become", which Matthew 4:19 does not. The change takes time, and the disciples are sent out in 6:7.

decisions.choice: {{gender:personas|hombres}}
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 4:19: Spanish has the same two wordings as English, "hombres" in the older sense of human beings or "personas" (meaning decision m3), so it keeps the gender setting.

decisions.choice: watu, no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Watu" already means people, men and women (meaning decision m3); "wanaume" would mean males only and change the meaning, so Swahili has no gender span here.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately having left the nets they followed him.

en.L: And immediately, leaving the nets, they followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They dropped their nets on the spot and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Right away they left their nets and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y al instante, dejando las redes, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.
es.B: En ese mismo momento soltaron sus redes y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.
es.R: Enseguida dejaron sus redes y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.

sw.L: Na mara moja, wakiziacha nyavu, walimfuata.
sw.B: Papo hapo waliziacha nyavu zao, wakamfuata.
sw.R: Mara moja waliacha nyavu zao, wakamfuata.

decisions.choice: followed him: went with him as his disciples
alternatives: walked behind him for a short time
decisions.reason: To follow a teacher was to become his disciple and share his life.

decisions.choice: immediately ... leaving: a response with no delay or conditions
decisions.reason: They leave their nets, their living, at once (see 10:28).

source.text: καὶ προβὰς ὀλίγον εἶδεν Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα, καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone on a little he saw James the [son] of the Zebedee and John the brother of him, and them in the boat mending the nets, \v 20 and immediately he called them.

en.L: And going on a little, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw James the [son] of Zebedee and John his brother, and they [were] in the boat mending the nets, \v 20 and immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called them.
en.B: He went on a little way and saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John, who were in their boat putting their nets in order. \v 20 He called them at once.
en.R: Jesus walked on a little farther and saw James and John, the sons of Zebedee. They were in their boat, fixing their fishing nets. \v 20 Right away Jesus called them to come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y avanzando un poco, vio a Santiago el [hijo] de Zebedeo y a Juan su hermano, y [a] ellos en la barca remendando las redes, \v 20 y al instante los llamó.
es.B: Un poco más adelante vio a Santiago, hijo de Zebedeo, y a su hermano Juan, que estaban en su barca poniendo en orden las redes. \v 20 Enseguida los llamó.
es.R: Jesús siguió caminando un poco más y vio a Santiago y a Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo. Estaban en su barca, arreglando sus redes de pesca. \v 20 Enseguida Jesús los llamó para que fueran con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Na akiendelea mbele kidogo, aliwaona Yakobo [mwana] wa Zebedayo na Yohana ndugu yake, nao [walikuwa] ndani ya mashua wakizitengeneza nyavu, \v 20 na mara moja akawaita.
sw.B: Alipoendelea mbele kidogo, aliwaona Yakobo mwana wa Zebedayo na Yohana ndugu yake, waliokuwa ndani ya mashua yao wakizitengeneza nyavu zao. \v 20 Mara akawaita.
sw.R: Yesu aliendelea kutembea mbele kidogo, akawaona Yakobo na Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo. Walikuwa ndani ya mashua yao wakitengeneza nyavu zao za kuvulia samaki. \v 20 Mara moja Yesu akawaita waje pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.

decisions.choice: mending: repairing or getting the nets ready
decisions.reason: The word means to put in order: to mend what is torn or to make the nets ready for use.

decisions.choice: the [son] of Zebedee: the article stands for "son"
decisions.reason: Greek often names a man by his father with the article alone. Zebedee is their father (1:20).

decisions.choice: called them: summoned them to be his disciples
decisions.reason: Jesus calls them as he called Simon and Andrew (1:17), and they follow (1:20).

decisions.choice: called them to come with him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the call was for, as in Matthew 4:21.

decisions.choice: Santiago
decisions.reason: The book-wide Spanish name for the apostle James, as in Matthew, the form most Spanish readers know; "Jacobo" is the older Bible form.

source.text: καὶ ἀφέντες τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν Ζεβεδαῖον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ τῶν μισθωτῶν ἀπῆλθον ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: and having left the father of them Zebedee in the boat with the hired men they went away after him.

en.L: And leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men, they went away after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers, they went off after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the workers he paid, and they went with Jesus.

es.L: Y habiendo dejado en la barca a su padre Zebedeo junto con los asalariados, se marcharon detrás de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Dejaron a su padre Zebedeo en la barca con los trabajadores a sueldo y se fueron tras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Dejaron a su padre Zebedeo en la barca con los hombres a los que él pagaba, y se fueron con Jesús.

sw.L: Na wakimwacha baba yao Zebedayo ndani ya mashua pamoja na vibarua, wakaondoka, wakaenda nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Walimwacha baba yao Zebedayo ndani ya mashua pamoja na vibarua, wakaondoka kumfuata.
sw.R: Walimwacha baba yao Zebedayo ndani ya mashua pamoja na wafanyakazi aliowalipa, wakaenda pamoja na Yesu.

decisions.choice: the hired men: Zebedee's paid workers
decisions.reason: Zebedee's fishing business had hired workers, so the sons did not leave their father alone, but they did leave a family business.

decisions.choice: went away after him: left to become his followers
alternatives: went on a short trip with him
decisions.reason: "After him" echoes "come after me" (1:17).

decisions.choice: went with Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what following meant, and names Jesus.

decisions.choice: vibarua
decisions.reason: "Kibarua" is a worker hired and paid for his labour, exactly the Greek word (meaning decision m1); Readable says it in a phrase, as the English does.

source.text: Καὶ εἰσπορεύονται εἰς Καφαρναούμ.

records.literal_gloss: And they go into Capernaum.

en.L: And they go into Capernaum.
en.B: They made their way to Capernaum.
en.R: Then they went to the town of Capernaum.

es.L: Y entran en Cafarnaúm.
es.B: Llegaron a Cafarnaúm.
es.R: Luego fueron al pueblo de Cafarnaúm.

sw.L: Na wanaingia Kapernaumu.
sw.B: Walifika Kapernaumu.
sw.R: Kisha walikwenda katika mji wa Kapernaumu.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: a fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Capernaum became the base of Jesus' work in Galilee (2:1).

decisions.choice: they go: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid.

decisions.choice: go (L); made their way (B); went (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Mark's present tense. Balanced and Readable use the past.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς τοῖς σάββασιν ἐδίδασκεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν.

records.literal_gloss: and immediately on the Sabbaths he was teaching into the synagogue.

en.L: And immediately on the Sabbath, [going] into the synagogue, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching.
en.B: On the Sabbath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went straight into the synagogue and taught there.
en.R: On the Sabbath, the weekly day of rest, Jesus went into the synagogue, where the Jews met to worship, and taught the people.

es.L: Y al instante, el sábado, [entrando] en la sinagoga, enseñaba.
es.B: El sábado fue directamente a la sinagoga y se puso a enseñar allí.
es.R: El sábado, el día semanal de descanso, Jesús entró en la sinagoga, donde los judíos se reunían para adorar a Dios, y enseñó a la gente.

sw.L: Na mara moja siku ya Sabato, [akiingia] ndani ya sinagogi, alikuwa akifundisha.
sw.B: Siku ya Sabato alikwenda moja kwa moja katika sinagogi, akafundisha humo.
sw.R: Siku ya Sabato, siku ya kupumzika kila juma, Yesu aliingia katika sinagogi, mahali Wayahudi walipokutana kumwabudu Mungu, akawafundisha watu.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbaths: on the Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The plural is the normal way of naming the Sabbath day, like the Hebrew. One day is meant, as the story that follows shows.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verb for entering
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "having gone into the synagogue, he was teaching". The SBLGNT text has only "into the synagogue", which still implies that he went in. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the synagogue: the meeting place for prayer and reading the law
decisions.reason: Jews met in the synagogue on the Sabbath to pray and to hear the scriptures read and explained. A visiting teacher could be asked to speak.

decisions.choice: he was teaching: he taught, and kept on teaching
alternatives: he had been teaching for a long time
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous, setting the scene for what happened while he taught (1:23).

decisions.choice: the weekly day of rest; where the Jews met to worship
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two words for readers who do not know them.

decisions.choice: el sábado
decisions.reason: "Sábado" is the Spanish name of the day and comes from the Hebrew word for the Sabbath, so it names the day plainly (meaning decision m1); Readable adds what it was, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ, ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And they were astonished at the teaching of him; he was for teaching them as authority having and not as the scribes.

en.L: And they were astonished at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching them as [one] having authority, and not as the scribes.
en.B: His teaching astounded them. Unlike the scribes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them as someone who has authority.
en.R: The people were amazed at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching. He did not teach like the teachers of God's law. He taught like someone who had real authority.

es.L: Y estaban asombrados de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza, pues estaba enseñándoles como [uno que] tiene autoridad, y no como los escribas.
es.B: Su enseñanza los dejó atónitos. A diferencia de los escribas, les enseñaba como alguien que tiene autoridad.
es.R: La gente estaba asombrada de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza. No enseñaba como los maestros de la ley de Dios. Enseñaba como alguien que tenía verdadera autoridad.

sw.L: Na walikuwa wakishangaa juu ya mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kwa maana alikuwa akiwafundisha kama [mmoja] aliye na mamlaka, na si kama wale waandishi.
sw.B: Mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yaliwashangaza sana. Tofauti na waandishi, aliwafundisha kama mtu mwenye mamlaka.
sw.R: Watu walishangazwa na mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Hakufundisha kama walimu wa sheria ya Mungu. Alifundisha kama mtu mwenye mamlaka ya kweli.

decisions.choice: astonished: struck with amazement
decisions.reason: The word means to be overwhelmed by something. It says nothing yet about whether they believed.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and the power to speak and act
decisions.reason: Jesus' authority is shown at once over an unclean spirit (1:27). His opponents later ask where his authority comes from (11:28).

decisions.choice: the scribes: experts in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The scribes taught the law and how to keep it, often by quoting earlier teachers. They become Jesus' opponents (2:6; 3:22).

decisions.choice: the teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: Readable uses a name that says what the scribes did, as in Matthew 2:4.

decisions.choice: los escribas (L, B); los maestros de la ley de Dios (R)
alternatives: los maestros de la ley at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide term (meaning decision m3): "escribas" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says who they were, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria ya Mungu (R)
alternatives: walimu wa sheria at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide term (meaning decision m3): "waandishi" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says who they were, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἦν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ καὶ ἀνέκραξεν λέγων· Τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ;

records.literal_gloss: And immediately there was in the synagogue of them a man in a spirit unclean, and he cried out \v 24 saying, What to us and to you, Jesus Nazarene?

en.L: And immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out, \v 24 saying, "What [is there] to us and to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Jesus of Nazareth?
en.B: Right then, in their synagogue, there was a man with an unclean spirit, and he screamed, \v 24 "What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth?
en.R: Right then a man with an evil spirit in him was in the synagogue. He shouted, \v 24 "Jesus from Nazareth, why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bothering us?

es.L: Y al instante había en la sinagoga de ellos un hombre con un espíritu impuro, y gritó, \v 24 diciendo: «¿Qué [hay] entre nosotros y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, Jesús nazareno?
es.B: En ese mismo momento había en la sinagoga de ellos un hombre con un espíritu impuro, que se puso a gritar: \v 24 «¿Qué tienes {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} que ver con nosotros, Jesús de Nazaret?
es.R: En ese momento estaba en la sinagoga un hombre que tenía dentro un espíritu maligno. El hombre gritó: \v 24 «Jesús de Nazaret, ¿por qué nos molestas?

sw.L: Na mara moja palikuwa katika sinagogi lao mtu mwenye pepo mchafu, naye akapiga kelele, \v 24 akisema, "Kuna nini kati yetu na {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Yesu Mnazareti?
sw.B: Wakati huo huo, katika sinagogi lao palikuwa na mtu aliyekuwa na pepo mchafu, akapiga yowe, \v 24 "Wewe una shughuli gani nasi, Yesu wa Nazareti?
sw.R: Wakati huo huo, katika sinagogi palikuwa na mtu mwenye pepo mbaya ndani yake. Akapiga kelele, \v 24 "Yesu wa Nazareti, kwa nini unatusumbua?

decisions.choice: with an unclean spirit: in the power of an unclean spirit
alternatives: a man who had a bad attitude
decisions.reason: "In a spirit" means held under the spirit's power. The spirit speaks through the man.

decisions.choice: an unclean spirit: an evil spirit, a demon
decisions.reason: Mark calls these beings both unclean spirits and demons (1:34; 3:22, 30). "Unclean" sets them against the Holy Spirit (1:8) and the Holy One of God (1:24).

decisions.choice: what to us and to you: what do we have in common? leave us alone
alternatives: what do you want from us, a friendly question
decisions.reason: The phrase keeps someone at a distance (Judges 11:12; 1 Kings 17:18). Here it is hostile.

decisions.choice: us: the spirit speaks for all the unclean spirits
alternatives: the man and the spirit together
decisions.reason: The spirit speaks for its kind, which Jesus has come to defeat (3:27).

decisions.choice: an evil spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says "evil", since "unclean" suggests dirt to new readers.

decisions.choice: un espíritu impuro (L, B); un espíritu maligno (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording (meaning decision m2): "impuro" keeps the language of ritual purity in today's Spanish, where "inmundo" sounds like filth; Readable says plainly that the spirit is evil, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: pepo mchafu (L, B); pepo mbaya (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording (meaning decision m2). "Pepo" is the Swahili word for an evil spirit; "roho" would be heard as a person's spirit or the Holy Spirit. Readable says plainly that it is evil, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἦλθες ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς;

records.literal_gloss: Did you come to destroy us?

en.L: Did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come to destroy us?
en.B: Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} here to destroy us?
en.R: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come to get rid of us?

es.L: ¿Viniste a destruirnos?
es.B: ¿Has venido a destruirnos?
es.R: ¿Has venido a acabar con nosotros?

sw.L: Ulikuja kutuangamiza?
sw.B: Je, umekuja kutuangamiza?
sw.R: Umekuja kutuondoa kabisa?

decisions.choice: a question, as the SBLGNT prints it
alternatives: a statement: You have come to destroy us!
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have no question marks, and the words can be read either way. The question fits the alarm of the other questions around it.

decisions.choice: destroy: the end of the evil spirits' power
decisions.reason: The spirit fears the judgment that God's kingdom brings on evil.

source.text: οἶδά σε τίς εἶ, ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: I know you who you are, the holy [one] of the God.

en.L: I know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are: the Holy One of God."
en.B: I know who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are: God's Holy One!"
en.R: I know who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. You are God's Holy One!"

es.L: Te conozco, quién eres: el Santo de Dios».
es.B: Sé quién eres: ¡el Santo de Dios!».
es.R: Yo sé quién eres. ¡Eres el Santo de Dios!».

sw.L: Ninakujua {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni nani, yule Mtakatifu wa Mungu."
sw.B: Ninajua {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni nani: ndiwe Mtakatifu wa Mungu!"
sw.R: Ninajua {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni nani. Wewe ndiwe Mtakatifu wa Mungu!"

decisions.choice: the Holy One of God: the one set apart and belonging to God
decisions.reason: The spirit, unclean, names Jesus as the one who is holy, belonging wholly to God (compare John 6:69).

decisions.choice: I know who you are: naming him to resist him
decisions.reason: Knowing and saying another's name was thought to give power over him. Jesus silences the spirit (1:25).

source.text: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Φιμώθητι καὶ ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And rebuked him the Jesus saying, Be silenced and come out of him.

en.L: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, "Be silenced, and come out of him!"
en.B: Jesus ordered it sternly, "Silence! Come out of the man!"
en.R: Jesus spoke strongly to the evil spirit. He said, "Be quiet! Come out of the man!"

es.L: Y Jesús lo reprendió, diciendo: «¡Enmudece y sal de él!».
es.B: Jesús le ordenó con severidad: «¡Silencio! ¡Sal de este hombre!».
es.R: Jesús le habló con fuerza al espíritu maligno. Le dijo: «¡Cállate! ¡Sal de ese hombre!».

sw.L: Na Yesu akamkemea, akisema, "Nyamaza, na umtoke!"
sw.B: Yesu alimkemea vikali, "Nyamaza! Mtoke mtu huyu!"
sw.R: Yesu alimkemea yule pepo mbaya kwa nguvu. Akasema, "Nyamaza! Mtoke mtu huyu!"

decisions.choice: rebuked: gave a stern command
decisions.reason: The word is used for Jesus' commands to spirits (3:12) and to the wind and sea (4:39). It is a word of power.

decisions.choice: be silenced: be muzzled, stop speaking
decisions.reason: The verb means to muzzle. Jesus will not let the spirit name him (1:34).

decisions.choice: him: the spirit is addressed; the man is the one it leaves
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the spirit and orders it out of the man.

decisions.choice: it; the man (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "it" for the spirit and "the man" for the one it is in, so that the two are not confused.

decisions.choice: enmudece
decisions.reason: The verb means to be muzzled, silenced by force (meaning decision m2); "enmudecer" keeps that sense, where "cállate" is an everyday "be quiet", kept for Readable.

source.text: καὶ σπαράξαν αὐτὸν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον καὶ φωνῆσαν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐξῆλθεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having convulsed him the spirit the unclean and having cried with a voice loud it came out of him.

en.L: And the unclean spirit, throwing him into convulsions and crying out with a loud voice, came out of him.
en.B: The unclean spirit threw the man into a fit, gave a loud shriek, and left him.
en.R: The evil spirit made the man shake hard. Then it gave a loud scream and came out of him.

es.L: Y tras convulsionarlo el espíritu impuro y dar un grito con voz fuerte, salió de él.
es.B: El espíritu impuro hizo que el hombre se retorciera en convulsiones, lanzó un fuerte alarido y salió de él.
es.R: El espíritu maligno hizo que el hombre se sacudiera con fuerza. Luego dio un grito muy fuerte y salió de él.

sw.L: Na yule pepo mchafu, baada ya kumtikisa kwa nguvu na kupaza sauti kubwa, alimtoka.
sw.B: Yule pepo mchafu alimtikisa mtu huyo kwa nguvu, akapiga ukelele mkubwa, akamtoka.
sw.R: Yule pepo mbaya alimtetemesha mtu huyo kwa nguvu. Kisha akapiga kelele kubwa, akamtoka.

decisions.choice: throwing into convulsions: shaking him violently
decisions.reason: The word describes a violent fit (9:26). The man is not harmed in the end.

decisions.choice: crying out: the spirit's last protest as it obeys
decisions.reason: The spirit cries out but has to leave, which the crowd notices (1:27).

source.text: καὶ ἐθαμβήθησαν ἅπαντες, ὥστε συζητεῖν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντας· Τί ἐστιν τοῦτο;

records.literal_gloss: And were amazed all, so that to discuss with themselves saying, What is this?

en.L: And they were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, "What is this?
en.B: Amazement seized them all, and they talked it over among themselves: "What is this?
en.R: All the people were amazed. They asked each other, "What is happening?

es.L: Y se asombraron todos, de modo que discutían entre sí, diciendo: «¿Qué es esto?
es.B: Todos quedaron asombrados, y lo comentaban entre ellos: «¿Qué es esto?
es.R: Toda la gente estaba asombrada. Se preguntaban unos a otros: «¿Qué está pasando?

sw.L: Na wote walishangaa mno, hivi kwamba walijadiliana wao kwa wao, wakisema, "Hili ni nini?
sw.B: Mshangao uliwashika wote, wakajadiliana wao kwa wao: "Hili ni nini?
sw.R: Watu wote walishangaa. Wakaulizana, "Ni nini kinachotokea?

decisions.choice: amazed: astonished, close to alarm
decisions.reason: The word is stronger than the one in 1:22 and has a sense of awe and fear.

decisions.choice: questioned among themselves: discussed and argued
decisions.reason: They talk it over with each other, trying to understand what they saw.

source.text: διδαχὴ καινή· κατ’ ἐξουσίαν καὶ τοῖς πνεύμασι τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις ἐπιτάσσει, καὶ ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: A teaching new with authority; even the spirits the unclean he commands, and they obey him.

en.L: A new teaching with authority! Even the unclean spirits {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commands, and they obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: A new kind of teaching, backed by authority! At {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} command even the unclean spirits do as they are told."
en.R: This man teaches something new, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} teaches with authority! He even tells evil spirits what to do, and they obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

es.L: ¡Una enseñanza nueva con autoridad! Incluso a los espíritus impuros {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} manda, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} obedecen».
es.B: ¡Una enseñanza de un tipo nuevo, y con autoridad! Hasta los espíritus impuros obedecen {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} órdenes».
es.R: ¡Este hombre enseña algo nuevo, y enseña con autoridad! Hasta les da órdenes a los espíritus malignos, y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} obedecen».

sw.L: Fundisho jipya lenye mamlaka! Hata pepo wachafu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anawaamuru, nao wanamtii."
sw.B: Ni fundisho jipya, lenye mamlaka! Kwa amri {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hata pepo wachafu wanatii."
sw.R: Mtu huyu anafundisha jambo jipya, tena anafundisha kwa mamlaka! Hata pepo wabaya anawaambia la kufanya, nao wanamtii!"

decisions.choice: with authority goes with the new teaching
alternatives: with authority he commands even the unclean spirits
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a break after "with authority", so the phrase describes the teaching. With the break before it, it describes the commands. Either way Jesus' word has authority.

decisions.choice: new: new in kind, not only recent
decisions.reason: The word means fresh or of a new kind. Teaching that drives out spirits by a word is something the people have not met before.

decisions.choice: even unclean spirits obey him: his word has God's power
decisions.reason: Jesus uses no ritual or name, only a command, and the spirits must obey.

source.text: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εὐθὺς πανταχοῦ εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον τῆς Γαλιλαίας.

records.literal_gloss: And went out the report of him immediately everywhere into all the surrounding region of the Galilee.

en.L: And the report about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} went out immediately everywhere, into the whole surrounding region of Galilee.
en.B: The news about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} went out at once in every direction, through all the country around Galilee.
en.R: Very quickly, people all over the area of Galilee heard about Jesus.

es.L: Y salió la noticia acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} al instante por todas partes, a toda la región de alrededor de Galilea.
es.B: Las noticias sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se extendieron enseguida en todas direcciones, por toda la comarca de Galilea.
es.R: Muy pronto, la gente de toda la región de Galilea oyó hablar de Jesús.

sw.L: Na habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zilitoka mara moja kila upande, kuingia eneo lote linalozunguka Galilaya.
sw.B: Habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zilienea mara moja pande zote, katika nchi yote ya kandokando ya Galilaya.
sw.R: Upesi sana watu kote katika eneo la Galilaya walisikia habari za Yesu.

decisions.choice: the surrounding region of Galilee: the whole region of Galilee round about
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means all of Galilee around Capernaum, though it could include lands beyond it.

decisions.choice: report: what people heard and told about him
decisions.reason: The word means something heard, news passed on by word of mouth.

source.text: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς ἐξελθόντες ἦλθον εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Σίμωνος καὶ Ἀνδρέου μετὰ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάννου.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately out of the synagogue having gone out they came into the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John.

en.L: And immediately, going out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
en.B: They left the synagogue and went straight to the house where Simon and Andrew lived, and James and John came with them.
en.R: Right after that, they left the synagogue and went to Simon and Andrew's house. James and John went with them.

es.L: Y al instante, saliendo de la sinagoga, fueron a la casa de Simón y Andrés, con Santiago y Juan.
es.B: Salieron de la sinagoga y se fueron directamente a la casa donde vivían Simón y Andrés, y Santiago y Juan fueron con ellos.
es.R: En cuanto salieron de la sinagoga, fueron a la casa de Simón y Andrés. Santiago y Juan fueron con ellos.

sw.L: Na mara moja, wakitoka katika sinagogi, walikwenda nyumbani kwa Simoni na Andrea, pamoja na Yakobo na Yohana.
sw.B: Walitoka katika sinagogi, wakaenda moja kwa moja nyumbani kwa Simoni na Andrea; Yakobo na Yohana nao walikwenda pamoja nao.
sw.R: Mara baada ya hapo, waliondoka katika sinagogi wakaenda nyumbani kwa Simoni na Andrea. Yakobo na Yohana walikwenda pamoja nao.

decisions.choice: they went out and came: the plural, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have the singular, with Jesus as the subject. With the plural, "they" are Jesus and the four disciples. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the house of Simon and Andrew: the brothers' home in Capernaum
alternatives: a house they rented for Jesus
decisions.reason: John 1:44 says the brothers came from Bethsaida; by now they lived in Capernaum, where Simon's family was.

source.text: ἡ δὲ πενθερὰ Σίμωνος κατέκειτο πυρέσσουσα, καὶ εὐθὺς λέγουσιν αὐτῷ περὶ αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And the mother-in-law of Simon was lying down fevering, and immediately they speak to him about her.

en.L: Now Simon's mother-in-law was lying down sick with a fever, and immediately they tell {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about her.
en.B: Simon's mother-in-law lay ill with a fever, and they lost no time in telling {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about her.
en.R: Simon's mother-in-law was lying in bed with a fever. Right away they told Jesus that she was sick.

es.L: Ahora bien, la suegra de Simón yacía con fiebre, y al instante {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hablan acerca de ella.
es.B: La suegra de Simón estaba en cama, enferma con fiebre, y sin perder tiempo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hablaron de ella.
es.R: La suegra de Simón estaba en cama con fiebre. Enseguida le contaron a Jesús que estaba enferma.

sw.L: Basi mama mkwe wa Simoni alikuwa amelala akiwa na homa, na mara moja wanamweleza juu yake.
sw.B: Mama mkwe wa Simoni alikuwa amelala kitandani akiugua homa, nao bila kukawia wakamweleza habari zake.
sw.R: Mama mkwe wa Simoni alikuwa kitandani, ana homa. Mara moja walimwambia Yesu kwamba alikuwa mgonjwa.

decisions.choice: Simon's mother-in-law: Simon was married
decisions.reason: Paul says that Peter took his wife with him on his travels (1 Corinthians 9:5).

decisions.choice: lying down with a fever: too ill to get up
decisions.reason: Fever could be a sign of serious illness, and she was in bed with it.

decisions.choice: they speak: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark tells this in the present tense to make it vivid.

source.text: καὶ προσελθὼν ἤγειρεν αὐτὴν κρατήσας τῆς χειρός· καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτὴν ὁ πυρετός, καὶ διηκόνει αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And having come to [her] he raised her having taken hold of the hand; and left her the fever, and she was serving them.

en.L: And coming to [her], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised her up, taking hold of [her] hand; and the fever left her, and she began serving them.
en.B: He came over, took hold of her hand, and lifted her up. Her fever was gone, and she started to look after them.
en.R: Jesus went to her. He took her hand and helped her get up. The fever went away, and she began to serve them food.

es.L: Y acercándose [a ella], la levantó, tomando [su] mano; y la fiebre la dejó, y se puso a servirles.
es.B: Él se acercó, la tomó de la mano y la levantó. La fiebre se le fue, y ella se puso a atenderlos.
es.R: Jesús fue a donde estaba ella. La tomó de la mano y la ayudó a levantarse. La fiebre se le quitó, y ella comenzó a servirles comida.
