sw.L: Naye akimkaribia, alimwinua, akiwa amemshika mkono; na homa ikamwacha, naye akawa akiwahudumia.
sw.B: Alimkaribia, akamwinua kwa kumshika mkono. Homa ikatoweka, naye akaanza kuwahudumia.
sw.R: Yesu alimwendea. Akamshika mkono, akamsaidia kuinuka. Homa ikaondoka, naye akaanza kuwaandalia chakula.

decisions.choice: raised her up: helped her to stand
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for raising the dead (5:41; 16:6), but here it means getting her up from her bed.

decisions.choice: serving them: looking after them as her guests
decisions.reason: She took up the work of a host, which shows that the cure was complete. The same verb is used of the angels in 1:13 and of Jesus himself in 10:45.

decisions.choice: she began serving: the imperfect describes what she went on doing
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: she got up and set about caring for them.

decisions.choice: serve them food
decisions.reason: Readable says what serving guests most likely meant here: giving them a meal.

source.text: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης, ὅτε ἔδυ ὁ ἥλιος, ἔφερον πρὸς αὐτὸν πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας καὶ τοὺς δαιμονιζομένους·

records.literal_gloss: Evening and having come, when set the sun, they were bringing to him all the [ones] badly having and the [ones] being demon-possessed.

en.L: Now when evening had come, when the sun set, they were bringing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all who were sick and those who were demon-possessed.
en.B: When evening came and the sun had set, people began bringing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everyone who was ill or controlled by demons.
en.R: That evening, after the sun went down, people brought all the sick to Jesus, and all who had demons in them.

es.L: Y llegada la tarde, cuando se puso el sol, iban trayendo hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a todos los que estaban mal y a los endemoniados.
es.B: Al anochecer, cuando ya se había puesto el sol, la gente {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} fue trayendo a todos los enfermos y a los que estaban dominados por demonios.
es.R: Esa tarde, después de que se puso el sol, la gente llevó a Jesús a todos los enfermos y a todos los que tenían demonios dentro.

sw.L: Basi jioni ilipoingia, jua lilipotua, walikuwa wakimletea wote waliokuwa wagonjwa na wale waliotawaliwa na pepo.
sw.B: Ilipofika jioni, jua likiisha kutua, watu walianza kumletea wote waliokuwa wagonjwa au waliotawaliwa na pepo.
sw.R: Jioni ile, baada ya jua kutua, watu walimletea Yesu wagonjwa wote, na wote waliokuwa na pepo ndani yao.

decisions.choice: when the sun set: the Sabbath ended at sunset
decisions.reason: The Sabbath of 1:21 ended at sunset. Then people could carry the sick without breaking the Sabbath rest.

decisions.choice: demon-possessed: under the control of demons
decisions.reason: Mark keeps the sick and the demon-possessed apart (1:34): illness is healed, demons are cast out.

decisions.choice: they were bringing: one after another
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: people kept bringing the sick.

source.text: καὶ ἦν ὅλη ἡ πόλις ἐπισυνηγμένη πρὸς τὴν θύραν.

records.literal_gloss: And was all the city gathered together at the door.

en.L: And the whole city was gathered together at the door.
en.B: The entire town had crowded together outside the door.
en.R: Almost everyone in the town crowded around the door of the house.

es.L: Y la ciudad entera estaba congregada junto a la puerta.
es.B: La gente de todo el pueblo se había amontonado ante la puerta.
es.R: Casi toda la gente del pueblo se juntó alrededor de la puerta de la casa.

sw.L: Na mji mzima ulikuwa umekusanyika pamoja kwenye mlango.
sw.B: Watu wa mji mzima walikuwa wamesongamana nje ya mlango.
sw.R: Karibu watu wote wa mji ule walijazana kuzunguka mlango wa nyumba.

decisions.choice: the whole city: a great crowd from the town
decisions.reason: "Whole" stresses how many came, as in 1:5.

decisions.choice: city: a town
decisions.reason: The word is used for any town with walls or a council. Capernaum was a lakeside town.

decisions.choice: town (B, R); city (L)
decisions.reason: Capernaum was small, so Balanced and Readable say "town". Readable says "almost everyone" to show the exaggeration.

decisions.choice: la gente de todo el pueblo (B, R); la ciudad entera (L)
decisions.reason: Capernaum was a town (meaning decision m2), so Balanced and Readable say "pueblo", as the English says "town". Spanish "todo el pueblo" alone could also mean "all the people of Israel", so they name the town's people.

source.text: καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ποικίλαις νόσοις, καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλεν, καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν λαλεῖν τὰ δαιμόνια, ὅτι ᾔδεισαν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And he healed many badly having various diseases and demons many he cast out, and not he was allowing to speak the demons, because they knew him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed many who were sick with various diseases, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cast out many demons; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not allowing the demons to speak, because they knew {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He cured many people who had diseases of every kind, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} threw out many demons. He did not permit the demons to say anything, since they knew {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus healed many people who had all kinds of sicknesses. He forced many demons to leave people. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not let the demons talk, because they knew who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.

es.L: Y curó a muchos que padecían diversas enfermedades, y muchos demonios expulsó; y no permitía que los demonios hablaran, porque {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conocían.
es.B: Curó a mucha gente que tenía enfermedades de toda clase, y echó fuera muchos demonios. No permitía que los demonios dijeran nada, ya que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} conocían.
es.R: Jesús sanó a muchas personas que tenían toda clase de enfermedades. También obligó a muchos demonios a salir de la gente. Pero no dejaba hablar a los demonios, porque sabían quién era {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Naye aliwaponya watu wengi waliokuwa wakiugua maradhi ya aina nyingi, na pepo wengi aliwafukuza; wala hakuwa akiwaacha pepo hao waseme, kwa kuwa walimfahamu.
sw.B: Aliponya watu wengi waliokuwa na magonjwa ya kila aina, akawatoa pepo wengi. Hakuwaruhusu pepo hao kusema lolote, kwa kuwa walimfahamu.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaponya watu wengi waliokuwa na kila aina ya magonjwa. Aliwalazimisha pepo wengi kuwatoka watu. Lakini hakuwaacha pepo hao waseme, kwa sababu walijua {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni nani.

decisions.choice: many: a great number, not a hint that some were left unhealed
decisions.reason: In Hebrew and Greek, "many" can stand for a large whole, as in 10:45. Matthew 8:16 says he healed all who were sick.

decisions.choice: he would not let the demons speak: he kept them from making him known
alternatives: he did not want to hear lies
decisions.reason: The demons knew who he was (1:24). Jesus silences them, as he does in 3:11-12, and makes himself known in his own way and time.

decisions.choice: they knew him, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "to be the Christ", likely from Luke 4:41. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: cast out: drove out with force
decisions.reason: This is the verb of 1:12, used for expelling demons by command.

decisions.choice: threw out (B); forced ... to leave (R)
decisions.reason: "Cast out" is old church language. Balanced uses an everyday verb with the same force.

source.text: Καὶ πρωῒ ἔννυχα λίαν ἀναστὰς ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κἀκεῖ προσηύχετο.

records.literal_gloss: And early in night very having risen he went out and went away into a solitary place, and there he was praying.

en.L: And very early, while still night, rising up, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out and went away into a deserted place, and there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was praying.
en.B: Long before daylight, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got up and went out. He went off to a lonely place and spent time there in prayer.
en.R: Very early the next morning, before it got light, Jesus got up and left the house. He went to a place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could be alone, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prayed there.

es.L: Y muy temprano, todavía de noche, habiéndose levantado, salió y se alejó hacia un lugar desierto, y allí estaba orando.
es.B: Mucho antes del amanecer, se levantó y salió. Se fue a un lugar apartado y pasó allí un tiempo en oración.
es.R: Al día siguiente, muy temprano, antes de que saliera el sol, Jesús se levantó y salió de la casa. Se fue a un lugar donde podía estar solo, y allí oró.

sw.L: Na asubuhi mapema sana, kungali usiku, aliamka akatoka, akaondoka kwenda mahali pa nyika, na huko akawa anaomba.
sw.B: Kabla kupambazuka kabisa, aliamka, akatoka nje. Akaenda mahali pa faragha, akakaa huko akiomba.
sw.R: Kesho yake asubuhi na mapema, kabla hakujapambazuka, Yesu aliamka akatoka nyumbani. Alikwenda mahali ambapo angeweza kuwa peke {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akaomba huko.

decisions.choice: very early, while still night: before dawn
decisions.reason: The three words together mean the last part of the night, before first light.

decisions.choice: a deserted place: the word for the wilderness of 1:3-13
decisions.reason: The place is "wilderness-like", empty of people. Jesus withdraws there to pray, as he will again (6:46; 14:32-39).

decisions.choice: he was praying: he spent time in prayer
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous; he was still praying when they found him (1:37).

decisions.choice: left the house
decisions.reason: Readable says where he went out from, Simon's house (1:29).

decisions.choice: un lugar desierto
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the link with "el desierto" of verses 3-13, as the Greek does (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable describe the place, as the English does.

decisions.choice: mahali pa nyika
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the link with "nyika" (the wilderness) of verses 3-13, as the Greek does (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable describe the place, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ κατεδίωξεν αὐτὸν Σίμων καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εὗρον αὐτὸν καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ ὅτι Πάντες ζητοῦσίν σε.

records.literal_gloss: And hunted down him Simon and those with him, \v 37 and found him and they say to him, All are seeking you.

en.L: And Simon and those with him searched hard for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 37 and they found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Everyone is looking for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: Simon and the others with him tracked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down. \v 37 Finding {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they said, "Everybody is out looking for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"
en.R: Simon and his friends went to look for Jesus. \v 37 They found {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All the people are looking for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} buscaron con empeño Simón y los que [estaban] con él, \v 37 y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} encontraron y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen: «Todos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} buscan».
es.B: Simón y los que estaban con él fueron siguiendo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} rastro. \v 37 Cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} encontraron, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¡Todo el mundo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} está buscando!».
es.R: Simón y sus amigos fueron a buscar a Jesús. \v 37 Cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} encontraron, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¡Toda la gente {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} está buscando!».

sw.L: Na Simoni na wale waliokuwa pamoja naye wakamtafuta kwa bidii, \v 37 nao wakamwona na wanamwambia, "Wote wanakutafuta."
sw.B: Simoni na wenzake walimfuatilia. \v 37 Walipomkuta, wakamwambia, "Kila mtu anakutafuta!"
sw.R: Simoni na rafiki zake walikwenda kumtafuta Yesu. \v 37 Walipomwona, walimwambia, "Watu wote wanakutafuta {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}!"

decisions.choice: searched hard for: hunted him down
decisions.reason: The verb means to pursue closely. They are eager to bring him back to the crowds.

decisions.choice: those with him: Andrew, James and John
decisions.reason: These are the others who were with Simon in 1:29.

decisions.choice: they say: the present tense of storytelling
decisions.reason: Mark tells this in the present tense to make it vivid.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἄγωμεν ἀλλαχοῦ εἰς τὰς ἐχομένας κωμοπόλεις, ἵνα καὶ ἐκεῖ κηρύξω, εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ἐξῆλθον.

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, Let us go elsewhere into the neighboring towns, so that also there I may proclaim; for this for I came out.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Let us go elsewhere, into the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim there also; for this is why I came out."
en.B: He replied, "Let us move on to the market towns nearby, so that I can proclaim the message there as well. This is what I came out to do."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Let us go to the other towns near here, so that I can tell people the good news there too. That is why I came."

es.L: Y les dice: «Vamos a otra parte, a los poblados vecinos, para que también allí proclame, porque para esto salí».
es.B: Él les respondió: «Sigamos hacia los pueblos de los alrededores, para que pueda proclamar el mensaje también allí. Para eso he salido».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Vamos a los otros pueblos que están cerca de aquí, para que allí también pueda anunciar la buena noticia. Para eso vine».

sw.L: Naye anawaambia, "Twendeni mahali pengine, katika miji iliyo jirani, ili nikatangaze huko pia; kwa maana kwa ajili ya hili nilitoka."
sw.B: Aliwajibu, "Twende kwenye miji ya soko iliyo karibu, ili nitangaze ujumbe huko pia. Hilo ndilo nililotoka kufanya."
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Twendeni kwenye miji mingine iliyo karibu, ili niwaeleze watu habari njema huko pia. Ndiyo sababu nilikuja."

decisions.choice: towns: market towns, larger than villages
decisions.reason: The word joins village and city: country towns with their own markets.

decisions.choice: I came out: from Capernaum, or from God who sent him
alternatives: I came out of the house this morning
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean that this is why he left the town, to preach elsewhere. Luke 4:43 says "I was sent", and the words may also hint at his mission from God.

decisions.choice: so that I may proclaim: his purpose is to preach, not only to heal
alternatives: so that I can heal there
decisions.reason: He leaves the crowd that came for healing and goes to proclaim the kingdom (1:14-15).

decisions.choice: tell people the good news
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus proclaimed, the good news of 1:14-15.

source.text: καὶ ἦλθεν κηρύσσων εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς αὐτῶν εἰς ὅλην τὴν Γαλιλαίαν καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλων.

records.literal_gloss: And he came proclaiming into the synagogues of them into all the Galilee and the demons casting out.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, proclaiming in their synagogues throughout all Galilee and casting out the demons.
en.B: He went into their synagogues all over Galilee, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} proclaimed the message and threw out demons.
en.R: Jesus went all over Galilee. He preached in their synagogues and forced demons to leave people.

es.L: Y fue proclamando en las sinagogas de ellos por toda Galilea, y echando fuera los demonios.
es.B: Recorrió las sinagogas de toda Galilea, donde proclamaba el mensaje y echaba fuera demonios.
es.R: Jesús recorrió toda Galilea. Predicaba en las sinagogas y obligaba a los demonios a salir de la gente.

sw.L: Naye alikuja akitangaza ndani ya masinagogi yao, kotekote Galilaya, na akiwafukuza wale pepo.
sw.B: Alizunguka katika masinagogi yao kote Galilaya, akatangaza ujumbe na kuwatoa pepo.
sw.R: Yesu alikwenda kila mahali katika Galilaya. Alihubiri katika masinagogi yao, akawalazimisha pepo kuwatoka watu.

decisions.choice: he came, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "he was preaching". The meaning is much the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a summary of his work: preaching and casting out demons
decisions.reason: Mark sums up a time of travel in a sentence; preaching and casting out demons go together, as in 3:14-15.

decisions.choice: threw out (B); forced ... to leave (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as in 1:34.

source.text: Καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτὸν λεπρὸς παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ γονυπετῶν λέγων αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.

records.literal_gloss: And comes to him a leper begging him and kneeling and saying to him, If you are willing you are able me to cleanse.

en.L: And a leper comes to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, begging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kneeling, and saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are willing, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able to cleanse me."
en.B: A man with a serious skin disease came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Falling on his knees, he pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are willing, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have the power to make me clean."
en.R: A man with leprosy, a bad skin disease, came to Jesus. He got down on his knees and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want to, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can heal me and make me clean!"

es.L: Y viene hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} un leproso, suplicándole y arrodillándose, y diciéndole: «Si quieres, puedes limpiarme».
es.B: Se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercó un hombre con una grave enfermedad de la piel. Cayendo de rodillas, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicó: «Si estás dispuesto, tienes poder para dejarme limpio».
es.R: Un hombre con lepra, una enfermedad grave de la piel, se acercó a Jesús. Se puso de rodillas y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogó: «¡Si quieres, puedes sanarme y dejarme limpio!».

sw.L: Na mkoma anakuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, akimsihi na kupiga magoti, akimwambia, "Kama unataka, unaweza kunitakasa."
sw.B: Mtu mmoja mwenye ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi alimjia. Akapiga magoti, akamsihi, "Ukiwa radhi, una uwezo wa kunifanya safi."
sw.R: Mtu mwenye ukoma, ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi, alimjia Yesu. Akapiga magoti, akamwomba, "Ukitaka, unaweza kuniponya na kunifanya safi!"

decisions.choice: leper: a person with a skin disease that made him unclean
decisions.reason: The word covered many skin diseases, which the law of Leviticus 13 tells the priests to judge. Not all were what is now called leprosy.

decisions.choice: unclean: he had to live apart from others
decisions.reason: A person with such a disease had to live outside the town and warn others away (Leviticus 13:45-46). Touching him made a person unclean.

decisions.choice: cleanse: heal the disease and make him clean before God's law
decisions.reason: Being cleansed meant the disease was gone and he could rejoin the community and its worship.

decisions.choice: and kneeling, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts do not have these words. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a man with a serious skin disease (B); a man with leprosy, a bad skin disease (R)
decisions.reason: "Leper" now sounds like a label for an outcast, and leprosy today names one disease. Balanced names the condition more broadly; Readable keeps the familiar word and explains it.

decisions.choice: kunitakasa (L); kunifanya safi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The man asks to be clean before the law as well as healed (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the one verb "kutakasa"; Balanced and Readable say "safi", as the English says "clean", and Readable adds "kuniponya", as the English Readable adds "heal".

source.text: καὶ ὀργισθεὶς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἥψατο καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι·

records.literal_gloss: And having become angry, having stretched out the hand of him he touched and says to him, I am willing, be cleansed.

en.L: And becoming angry, stretching out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched [him] and says to him, "I am willing; be cleansed."
en.B: Stirred with anger, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and touched him. "I am willing," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told him. "Be made clean!"
en.R: Jesus was angry. He put out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and touched the man. He said, "I do want to. Be healed and clean!"

es.L: Y enojándose, extendiendo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano, [lo] tocó y le dice: «Quiero; queda limpio».
es.B: Movido por el enojo, extendió {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano y tocó al hombre. «Quiero», le dijo. «¡Queda limpio!».
es.R: Jesús se enojó. Extendió {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano y tocó al hombre. Le dijo: «Sí quiero. ¡Queda sano y limpio!».

sw.L: Naye akiwa amekasirika, akinyoosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, alimgusa na kumwambia, "Nataka; takasika."
sw.B: Akiwa ameghadhibika, alinyoosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akamgusa. Akamwambia, "Nataka. Uwe safi!"
sw.R: Yesu alikasirika. Akanyoosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akamgusa yule mtu. Akasema, "Ndiyo, nataka. Pona, uwe safi!"

decisions.choice: becoming angry, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts read "moved with compassion". A few, including Codex Bezae and some Old Latin copies, read "becoming angry", which the SBLGNT prints. Scribes were more likely to soften anger into compassion than the reverse, and Mark speaks of Jesus' anger elsewhere (3:5; 10:14). Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: angry: Mark does not say at what
alternatives: angry at the disease and the evil behind it
decisions.reason: Jesus' anger may be at the disease and its power over the man, or at a world that shut him out. Nothing in the story says he is angry with the man, whom he heals at once.

decisions.choice: he touched him: he touched a man the law called unclean
decisions.reason: Touching an unclean person made one unclean (Leviticus 5:3). Here cleanness passes from Jesus to the man instead.

decisions.choice: I am willing: the answer to "if you are willing"
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the man's own word (1:40).

decisions.choice: touched him (B); touched the man (R)
decisions.reason: Greek can leave out the object; English needs it.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἡ λέπρα, καὶ ἐκαθαρίσθη.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately went away from him the leprosy, and he was cleansed.

en.L: And immediately the leprosy went away from him, and he was made clean.
en.B: In that moment the disease was gone from him, and he was clean.
en.R: Right away the skin disease went away, and the man was healed and clean.

es.L: Y al instante la lepra se apartó de él, y fue limpiado.
es.B: En ese mismo instante la enfermedad desapareció, y quedó limpio.
es.R: Enseguida la enfermedad de la piel se le quitó, y el hombre quedó sano y limpio.

sw.L: Na mara moja ukoma ukamwondoka, naye akatakaswa.
sw.B: Papo hapo ugonjwa ule ukamtoka, naye akawa safi.
sw.R: Mara moja ule ugonjwa wa ngozi ukatoweka, na yule mtu akapona, akawa safi.

decisions.choice: he was cleansed: made clean by God's act through Jesus' word
decisions.reason: The passive verb answers Jesus' command "be cleansed" (1:41).

decisions.choice: immediately: the cure was instant and complete
decisions.reason: The disease left at once, before the priest could examine him.

source.text: καὶ ἐμβριμησάμενος αὐτῷ εὐθὺς ἐξέβαλεν αὐτόν, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὅρα μηδενὶ μηδὲν εἴπῃς, ἀλλὰ ὕπαγε σεαυτὸν δεῖξον τῷ ἱερεῖ καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου ἃ προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And having sternly charged him immediately he sent away him, \v 44 and says to him, See nothing to no one you say, but go yourself show to the priest and offer for the cleansing of you what commanded Moses, for a testimony to them.

en.L: And sternly warning him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} immediately sent him away \v 44 and says to him, "See [that] you say nothing to anyone, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
en.B: Jesus gave him a stern warning and sent him away at once. \v 44 "Be sure you tell no one about this," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "Instead, go and let the priest examine you. Then offer what Moses required for your cleansing. That will be evidence to them."
en.R: Jesus quickly sent him away with a strong warning. \v 44 He said, "Do not tell anyone about this. Go and show yourself to the priest. Then give the offering that Moses commanded for people who are made clean. That will prove to them that you are clean."

es.L: Y tras advertirle con dureza, al instante lo hizo salir, \v 44 y le dice: «Cuidado, que a nadie digas nada; al contrario, anda, muéstrate al sacerdote y ofrece por tu purificación lo que ordenó Moisés, como testimonio para ellos».
es.B: Jesús le dio una severa advertencia y lo despidió enseguida. \v 44 «Asegúrate de no contarle esto a nadie», le dijo. «Más bien, ve y deja que el sacerdote te examine. Después ofrece lo que Moisés ordenó para tu purificación. Eso les servirá de prueba».
es.R: Jesús le dio una advertencia muy seria y lo despidió enseguida. \v 44 Le dijo: «No le cuentes esto a nadie. Ve y preséntate ante el sacerdote. Después da la ofrenda que mandó Moisés para los que quedan limpios. Eso les demostrará que estás limpio».

sw.L: Naye akiwa amemwonya kwa ukali, mara moja alimfukuza aende zake, \v 44 na anamwambia, "Hakikisha humwambii mtu yeyote chochote; badala yake, nenda ujionyeshe kwa kuhani, na utoe kwa ajili ya utakaso wako yale aliyoagiza Musa, yawe ushuhuda kwao."
sw.B: Yesu alimwonya vikali, akamwambia aondoke mara moja. \v 44 Akamwambia, "Hakikisha humwambii mtu yeyote habari hii. Badala yake, nenda kwa kuhani akuchunguze. Kisha utoe sadaka aliyoiagiza Musa kwa ajili ya kutakaswa kwako. Hiyo itakuwa ushahidi kwao."
sw.R: Yesu alimwonya kwa nguvu, akamwambia aondoke haraka. \v 44 Akasema, "Usimwambie mtu yeyote habari hii. Nenda ukajionyeshe kwa kuhani. Kisha utoe sadaka ambayo Musa aliiagiza kwa ajili ya watu waliotakaswa. Hiyo itawathibitishia kwamba wewe ni safi."

decisions.choice: sternly warning: speaking with deep feeling and force
decisions.reason: The word describes strong emotion, at times a snort of anger (14:5). Here it gives force to the warning that follows.

decisions.choice: sent him away: sent him out at once
decisions.reason: This is the verb of 1:12 and 1:34. It shows urgency, not anger at the man.

decisions.choice: show yourself to the priest: the law of Leviticus 14
decisions.reason: A priest examined a person healed of a skin disease and declared him clean. Then the person offered the sacrifices the law of Moses set out, and could return to the community.

decisions.choice: as a testimony to them: proof to the priests and people that he is clean
decisions.reason: "To them" most likely means the priests and the people. The words can also carry a warning, as in 6:11 and 13:9.

decisions.choice: tell no one: Jesus does not want to be known as a healer only
alternatives: a test of the man's obedience
decisions.reason: Jesus keeps his work quiet, as with the demons (1:34), and the man's report soon stops him entering towns (1:45).

decisions.choice: evidence (B); prove to them that you are clean (R)
decisions.reason: "Testimony" sounds like a speech in English; the word here means proof.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἐξελθὼν ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν πολλὰ καὶ διαφημίζειν τὸν λόγον, ὥστε μηκέτι αὐτὸν δύνασθαι φανερῶς εἰς πόλιν εἰσελθεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἔξω ἐπ’ ἐρήμοις τόποις ἦν· καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν πάντοθεν.

records.literal_gloss: But he having gone out began to proclaim much and to spread abroad the word, so that no longer him to be able openly into city to enter, but outside in solitary places he was; and they were coming to him from everywhere.

en.L: But he went out and began to proclaim [it] freely and to spread the word abroad, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was no longer able to enter a town openly, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was outside in deserted places; and they kept coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from everywhere.
en.B: But the man went off and began telling everyone, spreading the news of what had happened, so much that Jesus could not go into any town openly anymore. He kept to deserted places out in the country, and still people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from every direction.
en.R: But the man went away and told many people what had happened. He spread the news everywhere. Because of this, Jesus could not go into a town where people could see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed out in lonely places. But people still came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from everywhere.

es.L: Pero él salió y se puso a proclamar[lo] mucho y a difundir la palabra, hasta tal punto que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ya no podía entrar abiertamente en ningún pueblo, sino que permanecía fuera, en lugares desiertos; y acudían a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} de todas partes.
es.B: Pero el hombre se fue y empezó a contárselo a todos, divulgando lo que había pasado, tanto que Jesús ya no podía entrar abiertamente en ningún pueblo. Se quedaba en lugares despoblados, en el campo, y aun así la gente acudía a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} de todas partes.
es.R: Pero el hombre se fue y les contó a muchas personas lo que había pasado. Difundió la noticia por todas partes. Por eso Jesús ya no podía entrar en un pueblo donde la gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} viera. Así que se quedaba en lugares solitarios. Pero aun así la gente venía a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} de todas partes.

sw.L: Lakini yule, alipotoka, alianza kutangaza mambo mengi na kulieneza neno hilo, hata {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakuweza tena kuingia mji wowote waziwazi, bali alikaa nje mahali pa nyika; na walikuwa wakimjia kutoka kila upande.
sw.B: Lakini yule mtu alienda, akaanza kumweleza kila mtu, akieneza habari ya yaliyotokea, hata Yesu hakuweza tena kuingia mjini waziwazi. Alikaa nje mahali pasipo na watu, na bado watu walimjia kutoka pande zote.
sw.R: Lakini yule mtu aliondoka, akawaambia watu wengi yaliyotokea. Alieneza habari hiyo kila mahali. Kwa sababu hiyo, Yesu hakuweza kuingia mjini mahali ambapo watu wangemwona. Basi alikaa nje mahali pasipo na watu. Lakini bado watu walimjia kutoka kila mahali.

decisions.choice: he went out: the man who was healed
decisions.reason: The subject changes to Jesus only in the next clause, "so that he was no longer able". Some read Jesus as the one proclaiming throughout, but the man's disobedience fits 1:44.

decisions.choice: the word: the matter, what had happened
decisions.reason: The word can mean the message (2:2), and Mark may play on it, since the man "proclaims" as John and Jesus do. Here it is the news of his healing.

decisions.choice: so that: the result of the man's talking
alternatives: the reason Jesus avoided towns from the start
decisions.reason: Because of the crowds, Jesus could no longer come into a town openly.

decisions.choice: deserted places: the word for wilderness again
decisions.reason: As in 1:35, Jesus is out where no one lives, and yet people come to him there, as they came to John (1:5).

decisions.choice: the man; Jesus
decisions.reason: Greek moves from one "he" to another. Balanced and Readable name each one.
